A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PAPO and contain readable methods, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Shared results and analyses can be matched across renaming and relocation, supporting a reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original GRPO/PAPO benchmark experiments, masking and regularization ablations, training dynamics, and manual error analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical results and adds DAPO, Qwen3-VL, NoisyRollout, OCR, robustness, attention, and error-analysis experiments.

M1.justification: The perception KL loss, masking, and double-entropy regularizer remain, but v5 adds a substantive DAPO-based instantiation, PAPO_D. Its procedure uses token-level loss averaging and dynamic sampling that excludes all-correct or all-wrong rollout groups (Appendix B). v1 evaluated GRPO and reference-KL removal, explicitly leaving full DAPO integration to future work.

E1.justification: ViRL39K training and the original eight reasoning benchmarks remain. v5 adds OCR-Bench-v2 for fine-grained visual-text perception and MMLU-Pro with irrelevant random-noise images, extending coverage to a distinct perception task and a strictly vision-independent reasoning scenario (Appendices K–L).

E2.justification: v5 adds evaluated DAPO baselines in Table 1, GRPO plus NoisyRollout in Table 2, and entropy-regularized DAPO in Table 10. These materially expand comparison beyond v1's GRPO-based controls; DAPO and NoisyRollout were previously discussed but not evaluated as these comparators.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Qwen3-VL-2B-thinking, DAPO settings with an upper clipping threshold of 0.28 and up to 20 dynamic-sampling retries, and new analysis protocols using 100-instance attention samples, 30-instance error samples per dataset, and a stated 60-case follow-up. The retained GRPO experiments keep two training epochs and avg@8 evaluation at temperature 1.0.

E4.justification: v5 adds attention visualizations and entropy analysis, errors distinguishing random from semantic masking, entropy-coefficient sensitivity, regularized-DAPO controls, irrelevant-image robustness, and follow-up of perception-error outcomes. These investigate mechanisms and failure boundaries beyond v1's existing masking, KL-weighting, and collapse analyses, which are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Collapse-comparison error bars and avg@8 accuracy reporting already appear in v1. v5 introduces no stated independent training-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval procedures, or significance tests. The added attention means and medians are descriptive results rather than new uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original high-weight PAPO results remain as PAPO_G: overall accuracies are still 49.92 and 61.66 for Qwen2.5-VL-3B and 7B. New DAPO/PAPO_D comparisons report 52.40/55.24 and 55.01/63.16, alongside Qwen3, NoisyRollout, OCR, robustness, and analysis results. Detailed low-weight PAPO benchmark rows are omitted, although aggregate ablations remain. These are mostly added comparisons, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds the formal token-normalized PAPO_D objective and its nondegenerate-reward sampling constraint. The original perception-KL formulation and masking mathematics remain substantively intact. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution of perception-aware optimization remains. The abstract and conclusion extend explicit applicability from GRPO to both GRPO and DAPO. The abstract's claimed overall gains expand from approximately 4.4% to 4.4–17.5%, and vision-dependent gains from approximately 8.0% to 8.0–19.1%, reflecting the added comparisons.

C2.justification: v5 adds interpretations connecting PAPO to attention allocation, masking-dependent perception, compatibility with rollout modifications, and robustness to irrelevant images. Appendix N qualifies the perception argument by explaining that correcting perception need not eliminate other reasoning errors. The conclusion also identifies uniform application of the loss to all tokens as a direction for refinement.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly specifies rollout batch size 384, five responses per prompt, and 80 GB GPU memory, while documenting new DAPO and Qwen3 configurations. Section 8 reports a source-code supplement with training and evaluation instructions. Much of the learning-rate, epoch, masking, hardware-count, and timing information was already present; the new disclosures do not establish changes to retained experiments.

R1.justification: The literature coverage is substantially revised: the standalone general-RLVR discussion is removed, while Appendix P adds comparisons including training-framework approaches such as Semi-off-Policy and Vision-SR1 and newer visual-reasoning systems. Appendix G additionally connects masking findings to masked autoencoders and masked visual modeling. The central positioning around optimization-level perception supervision remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method presentation, and results narrative are extensively reorganized around GRPO and DAPO instantiations. Implementation details, reference-KL experiments, computational overhead, and much collapse analysis move into an expanded appendix structure. v5 also adds an appendix contents page and reproducibility, ethics, and LLM-use statements.

P2.justification: v5 switches from a two-column layout to a single-column conference format, revises the method schematic to display entropy regularization, and expands the main results table and training plots. It adds attention and error-outcome graphics and several comparison tables. Existing masking illustrations and collapse figures are relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v5 substantially strengthens evidence for portability and robustness beyond v1's GRPO-centered evaluation through DAPO controls, Qwen3, OCR, irrelevant-image testing, and targeted mechanism analyses. The entropy-regularized DAPO control is particularly useful: its 62.27 overall accuracy places PAPO_D's 63.16 in better context than the unstable baseline's 55.01. New reporting inconsistencies weaken Appendix N/Figure 15—the outcome counts total 59 despite a stated sample of 60—but do not outweigh the broader, more diagnostic validation.
